docs.t: D. Mass. — Same-day e-filing cutoff: 6:00 p.m.
docs.x: D. Mass.. Same-day e-filing cutoff: 6:00 p.m.. ECF is open around the clock, but a filing must be completed before 6:00 p.m. local time to count as filed that day. Most federal courts use midnight. (L.R. 5.4(d))

docs.t: D. Mass. — Put everything in the opening brief
docs.x: D. Mass.. Put everything in the opening brief. There is no reply as of right, except on summary judgment. Put every argument in the opening motion, because you may never get another word. Check the judge’s session order: some allow short replies, some bar sur-replies. (LR 7.1(b)(3))

docs.t: D. Mass. — Discovery is capped, and the client signs extension requests
docs.x: D. Mass.. Discovery is capped, and the client signs extension requests. 10 depositions, 25 interrogatories, 25 admissions, and only 2 sets of document requests per side. Parties can’t stipulate to extend response times, and requests to extend discovery or postpone trial must be signed by the lawyer and the client. (LR 26.1(c); LR 26.2(b))

docs.t: D. Mass. — Some things happen without a court order
docs.x: D. Mass.. Some things happen without a court order. No proof of service by day 90 plus a good-cause motion by day 104, and the clerk dismisses. No certified state court record within 42 days of removal, and the case goes back. (LR 4.1; LR 81.1)

docs.t: D. Mass. — Discovery motions follow LR 37.1’s procedure
docs.x: D. Mass.. Discovery motions follow LR 37.1’s procedure. Movant arranges the conference; the other side has 7 days to answer the request; item-by-item memorandum; 14 calendar days to respond to the motion; certificate in the margin of the last page. (LR 37.1)

docs.t: D.P.R. — Pay bar renewal fees by October 1 every year
docs.x: D.P.R.. Pay bar renewal fees by October 1 every year. To stay in good standing, pay the annual bar membership renewal fee on or before October 1. Lawyers who don’t lose CM/ECF access and eligibility for criminal and pro bono appointments. docs.x: W.D. Tenn.. 20 pages, and replies need leave. Memoranda for and against a motion can’t exceed 20 pages, and a reply can’t exceed 5. On ordinary motions a reply is allowed only if the court grants a motion for leave, which must be filed within 7 days of service of the response. (LR 7.2(e), (c))

docs.t: W.D. Tenn. — 14 days to respond, 28 for motions to dismiss and summary judgment
docs.x: W.D. Tenn.. 14 days to respond, 28 for motions to dismiss and summary judgment. Respond to most motions within 14 days after service. A response to a Rule 12(b) or 12(c) motion is due in 28 days, and a response to a summary judgment motion in 28 days or when a responsive pleading is due, whichever is later. (LR 7.2(a)(2); 12.1(b); 56.1(b))

docs.t: W.D. Tenn. — Certificate of consultation, or the motion can be denied
docs.x: W.D. Tenn.. Certificate of consultation, or the motion can be denied. Every motion except those under Rules 12, 56, 59 and 60, discovery motions included, needs a certificate saying you consulted and couldn’t reach accord, or all agree. Name the participating lawyers and the date and manner. The movant starts the conference and gives reasonable notice. Skipping the certificate can be good grounds for denial. (LR 7.2(a)(1)(B))

docs.t: W.D. Tenn. — Proposed order goes to the judge’s ECF mailbox
docs.x: W.D. Tenn.. Proposed order goes to the judge’s ECF mailbox. All motions except those under Rules 12, 56, 59 and 60 come with a proposed order in a word processing format, sent only to the presiding judge’s ECF mailbox, not the regular email address. (LR 7.2(a)(1)(A))

docs.t: W.D. Tenn. — Silence can lose the motion
docs.x: W.D. Tenn.. Silence can lose the motion. Failing to respond on time to a motion other than one to dismiss may be deemed good grounds for granting it. (LR 7.2(a)(2))

docs.t: W.D. Tenn. — Summary judgment: 10-page fact statement, answered fact by fact
docs.x: W.D. Tenn.. Summary judgment: 10-page fact statement, answered fact by fact. The movant files a separate, numbered statement of facts with record citations, up to 10 pages. The opponent answers each fact right below it as undisputed, undisputed for this motion only, or disputed with a citation. Missing the deadline means the facts are treated as undisputed. (LR 56.1)

docs.t: W.D. Tenn. — Reconsidering an interim order is narrow
docs.x: W.D. Tenn.. Reconsidering an interim order is narrow. Motions to reconsider interlocutory orders are allowed only as motions for revision under Rule 54(b). You must show a material new fact or law you couldn’t earlier know, new facts or a change in law, or a manifest failure to consider material arguments. No repeating old arguments, on pain of sanctions. (LR 7.3)

docs.t: W.D. Tenn. — No continuance by stipulation

docs.t: M.D. Tenn. — Seal in two steps: motion first, document second
docs.x: M.D. Tenn.. Seal in two steps: motion first, document second. File a motion for leave to file under seal and do NOT attach the document. docs.t: M.D. Tenn. — Sealing needs compelling reasons, document by document
docs.x: M.D. Tenn.. Sealing needs compelling reasons, document by document. The motion must overcome the presumption that records are public and show the sealing is narrowly tailored, analyzing each document with facts and authority. An unopposed motion or agreed order that skips the standard doesn’t comply. (LR 5.03(c))

docs.t: M.D. Tenn. — Discovery fights start with a joint statement
docs.x: M.D. Tenn.. Discovery fights start with a joint statement. Before a motion to compel, to quash, or for a protective order, confer in good faith. docs.t: E.D. Tenn. — Silence can be treated as waiver
docs.x: E.D. Tenn.. Silence can be treated as waiver. Failure to respond to a motion may be deemed a waiver of any opposition to the relief sought. The court can also act before the response time runs out in exceptional circumstances. (LR 7.2)

docs.x: E.D. Tenn.. Discovery motions quote the discovery. A discovery motion must recite word for word each interrogatory, request, answer, response and objection at issue, or attach the discovery document. (LR 37.2)

docs.x: M.D. La.. 21 days to respond to a motion. File the response, with opposing affidavits and supporting documents then available, within 21 days after service. The court can set a shorter or longer time for good cause. (LR 7(f))

docs.t: D. Neb. — The court’s generative AI rule: verify everything
docs.x: D. Neb.. The court’s generative AI rule: verify everything. You are responsible for the accuracy of quotations, citations, paraphrases, and analysis whether or not AI drafted them. docs.x: D. Neb.. Word limits, not page limits: 13,000 and 6,500. docs.t: D. Neb. — Twenty-one days to oppose dispositive-type motions, fourteen for the rest
docs.x: D. Neb.. Twenty-one days to oppose dispositive-type motions, fourteen for the rest. Any other motion gets 14 days. (NECivR 7.1(b)(1)(B))

docs.t: D. Neb. — Failing to oppose forfeits your side of the facts

docs.t: D. Neb. — The brief must be separate from the motion and from the evidence
docs.x: D. Neb.. The brief must be separate from the motion and from the evidence. A motion raising a substantial issue of law needs its own brief, filed with the motion and not attached to or incorporated in it. Failing to brief an issue may be treated as a waiver, and not following the rule may be treated as abandoning your position. (NECivR 7.1(a)(1)(A))

docs.t: D. Neb. — Evidence goes in separately with an index
docs.x: D. Neb.. Evidence goes in separately with an index. Evidentiary materials are filed separately with an evidence index listing each item and the related motion. docs.t: D. Neb. — Summary judgment: a separate statement of facts, with page and line cites

docs.t: D. Neb. — A judge can require a resident lawyer with full authority
docs.x: D. Neb.. A judge can require a resident lawyer with full authority. A judge may require a nonresident lawyer to associate with a lawyer who lives in the district and is a member of this bar. docs.t: W.D. Wis. — Only five local rules: the judge’s procedures do the rest
docs.x: W.D. Wis.. Only five local rules: the judge’s procedures do the rest. The local rules cover admission, magistrate judges, ADR, juror contact, and e-filing. Briefing deadlines, page limits, and motion practice come from the Federal Rules and each judge’s own procedures, so read those before you file. (W.D. Wis. LR 1 through 5)

docs.t: W.D. Wis. — Everything is e-filed, with narrow paper exceptions
docs.x: W.D. Wis.. Everything is e-filed, with narrow paper exceptions. All civil and criminal documents must be filed electronically. Paper is allowed only for administrative records, state court records and transcripts, criminal case-initiating documents, trial exhibits, pro se filings by non-Filing Users, juvenile criminal matters, and highly sensitive documents. (W.D. Wis. E-Filing Procedures II.B, II.C)

docs.t: W.D. Wis. — Open a civil case one way, never both
docs.x: W.D. Wis.. Open a civil case one way, never both. Either email the clerk for a shell case number, or use the self-serve option in CM/ECF. The procedures say do not do both. A lawsuit is not filed until your complaint or notice of removal shows on the docket. (W.D. Wis. E-Filing Procedures IV.A)

docs.t: W.D. Wis. — Briefs, affidavits, and declarations are separate docket entries
docs.x: W.D. Wis.. Briefs, affidavits, and declarations are separate docket entries. File each one as its own docket entry, not as an attachment to a motion. Exhibits are separate attachments with descriptive titles. (W.D. Wis. E-Filing Procedures V.C)

docs.t: W.D. Wis. — PDFs: no passwords, 35 MB maximum
docs.x: W.D. Wis.. PDFs: no passwords, 35 MB maximum. Larger files must be filed in pieces, each under 35 MB. Password-protected or encrypted PDFs are rejected. (W.D. Wis. E-Filing Procedures III.A)

docs.t: W.D. Wis. — Consider ADR within 30 days of the defendants’ appearance
docs.x: W.D. Wis.. Consider ADR within 30 days of the defendants’ appearance. Litigants must consider alternative dispute resolution within 30 days of defendants’ appearance. The clerk mediates civil cases at no charge. Pro se plaintiff cases, collection and U.S. mortgage foreclosure actions, social security appeals, and bankruptcy matters (except adversary proceedings) are exempt. (W.D. Wis. LR 16.6(A))

docs.t: W.D. Wis. — You must redact, and keep the unredacted copy for two years
docs.x: W.D. Wis.. You must redact, and keep the unredacted copy for two years. Use only the last four digits of SSNs and account numbers, initials for minors, birth year only, and city and state for home addresses in criminal filings. The clerk does not check. Keep the unredacted version for two years after the appeal period ends. (W.D. Wis. E-Filing Procedures VI.A)

docs.t: W.D. Wis. — Sealing follows Administrative Order 460
docs.x: W.D. Wis.. Sealing follows Administrative Order 460. Use the “Motion to Seal” event. If it is denied, the documents are unsealed and public. Don’t move to seal a document already covered by a protective order. (W.D. Wis. E-Filing Procedures VI.B)

docs.t: W.D. Wis. — Jury instructions also go to chambers by email
docs.x: W.D. Wis.. Jury instructions also go to chambers by email. Send proposed instructions and the verdict form in Word or WordPerfect to the judge’s chambers address, with the case number in the subject and file name. (W.D. Wis. E-Filing Procedures V.B)

docs.t: W.D. Wis. — A technical failure is not an excuse for your own equipment
docs.x: W.D. Wis.. A technical failure is not an excuse for your own equipment. Only a failure of the ECF website counts. If it caused a late filing, file a declaration with any error message, and file on the first day the court is open after the deadline. (W.D. Wis. E-Filing Procedures III.G)

docs.t: W.D. Wis. — Filing deadline: midnight, local time
docs.x: W.D. Wis.. Filing deadline: midnight, local time. On the last day, an electronic filing is timely until midnight in the court’s time zone. Paper filings are due when the clerk’s office is scheduled to close. Some judges set an earlier time in their standing orders, so check yours. (Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(a)(4)(A))

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — The first 28-day extension is a notice, not a motion
docs.x: S.D. Ind.. The first 28-day extension is a notice, not a motion. Initial extensions of a pleading response or a discovery response must be made by a Notice of Parties’ First Extension of Time, with no proposed order, unless a party objects. It can’t exceed 28 days, must confirm no earlier extension and no conflict with court deadlines, and must report each other party’s agreement or your attempts to reach them. (S.D. Ind. L.R. 6-1(a))

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — Thirty-page briefs, fifteen-page replies, cut in 2024
docs.x: S.D. Ind.. Thirty-page briefs, fifteen-page replies, cut in 2024. Supporting and response briefs may not exceed 30 pages, excluding tables, appendices, and certificates of service. Replies may not exceed 15 pages. The limit was reduced in July 2024. (S.D. Ind. L.R. 7-1(e))

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — Twenty-one days for Rule 12 motions, fourteen for others
docs.x: S.D. Ind.. Twenty-one days for Rule 12 motions, fourteen for others. A response to a Rule 12(b), (e), or (f) motion is due 21 days after service, unless you amend as of course. Everything else is 14 days. Replies are 7 days. The court may rule summarily if no response is filed. (S.D. Ind. L.R. 7-1(c))

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — Don’t bury a motion inside a brief
docs.x: S.D. Ind.. Don’t bury a motion inside a brief. A motion must not be contained in a brief, response, or reply to another motion unless the court orders it. (S.D. Ind. L.R. 7-1(a))

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — Summary judgment: 28 days to respond, and a surreply only for new evidence
docs.x: S.D. Ind.. Summary judgment: 28 days to respond, and a surreply only for new evidence. The response and evidence are due 28 days after service and reply 14 days after that. A surreply is allowed only if the reply cites new evidence or objects to your evidence, within 7 days, limited to those issues. (S.D. Ind. L.R. 56-1(b), (d))

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — Facts live inside the brief, and they count against your pages
docs.x: S.D. Ind.. Facts live inside the brief, and they count against your pages. There is no separate fact statement. The brief must contain a “Statement of Material Facts Not in Dispute,” and the response a “Statement of Material Facts in Dispute.” Each fact needs a record cite to a page or paragraph, and the court has no duty to search the record. (S.D. Ind. L.R. 56-1(a), (b))

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — Unrebutted facts are admitted without controversy
docs.x: S.D. Ind.. Unrebutted facts are admitted without controversy. The court assumes the movant’s supported facts are admitted unless the non-movant specifically controverts them with admissible evidence. (S.D. Ind. L.R. 56-1(f))

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — No motions to strike during summary judgment
docs.x: S.D. Ind.. No motions to strike during summary judgment. Raise objections to evidence in your brief. Collateral motions are disfavored. (S.D. Ind. L.R. 56-1(i))

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — Costs and fees: both within 14 days of final judgment
docs.x: S.D. Ind.. Costs and fees: both within 14 days of final judgment. You can’t recover attorney’s fees and costs unless you file a bill of costs and a fee motion within 14 days after final judgment. An extension requires a motion filed before the deadline. (S.D. Ind. L.R. 54-1(a))

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — Call the magistrate judge before a discovery motion
docs.x: S.D. Ind.. Call the magistrate judge before a discovery motion. After a good-faith conference fails, contact the magistrate judge’s chambers to see if a phone conference can resolve the dispute before you file. A deposition objection that threatens the deposition lets you recess to call chambers. (S.D. Ind. L.R. 37-1(a))

docs.t: S.D. Ind. — Fee, Rule 11, and disqualification motions need a conference statement
docs.x: S.D. Ind.. Fee, Rule 11, and disqualification motions need a conference statement. The court may not grant these motions without a statement of reasonable efforts to confer, with the date, time, and place of every conference and everyone who took part. (S.D. Ind. L.R. 7-1(g))

docs.t: N.D. Ind. — A 28-day automatic extension, by notice, once
docs.x: N.D. Ind.. A 28-day automatic extension, by notice, once. The deadline to respond to a pleading or discovery request is extended automatically by filing a notice, if it was not extended before, the extension is 28 days or less, and the notice states the old and new deadlines and that everyone you could reach agreed. It is not available when a party is unrepresented. (N.D. Ind. L.R. 6-1(b))

docs.x: N.D. Ind.. Twenty-one days to respond to a Rule 12 motion, fourteen for everything else. Responses to Rule 12 motions are due 21 days after service, unless you first amend as of course. docs.t: N.D. Ind. — Twenty-five pages for briefs, fifteen for replies
docs.x: N.D. Ind.. Twenty-five pages for briefs, fifteen for replies. Supporting and response briefs ordinarily can’t exceed 25 pages, excluding tables and appendices, and replies can’t exceed 15. A brief over 25 pages (allowed only for extraordinary and compelling reasons) must include a table of contents, an issue statement, and a table of authorities. (N.D. Ind. L.R. 7-1(e))

docs.t: N.D. Ind. — Summary judgment: a separate fact statement, and a 28-day response
docs.x: N.D. Ind.. Summary judgment: a separate fact statement, and a 28-day response. The movant files a motion, a brief, and a Statement of Material Facts with numbered paragraphs and record cites. The opponent has 28 days to file a brief and a Response that restates each paragraph verbatim, answers it, and cites evidence for every dispute. (N.D. Ind. L.R. 56-1(a), (b))

docs.t: N.D. Ind. — No motion to strike on summary judgment
docs.x: N.D. Ind.. No motion to strike on summary judgment. Raise disputes about admissibility or materiality in your briefs. A separate motion to strike must not be filed. (N.D. Ind. L.R. 56-1(f))

docs.t: N.D. Ind. — A Rule 12 defense is ignored until you file a motion and brief
docs.x: N.D. Ind.. A Rule 12 defense is ignored until you file a motion and brief. Motions under Rules 12, 37, 56, and 65(b) need a supporting brief. The court will not rule on a Rule 12 defense until the party who raised it files a motion and brief. (N.D. Ind. L.R. 7-1(b), (c))

docs.t: N.D. Ind. — Costs: file AO 133 within 14 days
docs.x: N.D. Ind.. Costs: file AO 133 within 14 days. To recover costs, file and serve a completed AO Form 133 within 14 days after final judgment. You can ask for more time for good cause, but only by motion filed before the deadline. (N.D. Ind. L.R. 54-1(a))

docs.t: N.D. Ind. — Discovery motions need a certification with date, time, place, and names

docs.x: N.D. Ind.. Oral argument is requested in a separate document. File a separate document explaining why argument is needed and how long it should take, with your supporting, response, or reply brief. No new evidence at argument. (N.D. Ind. L.R. 7-5(a))

docs.t: D.S.D. — Twenty-one days to oppose, fourteen to reply; briefs capped at 30 pages
docs.x: D.S.D.. Twenty-one days to oppose, fourteen to reply; briefs capped at 30 pages. An opposed motion raising a question of law needs a brief. The response is due 21 calendar days after the motion and brief are served, and the reply 14 calendar days after the response. docs.t: D.S.D. — Local counsel must attend everything, even by phone
docs.x: D.S.D.. Local counsel must attend everything, even by phone. Pro hac vice lawyers need local counsel who signs and files all documents and is present at every proceeding, including telephone and video conferences, unless the court orders otherwise. (D.S.D. Civ. LR 83.2(E))

docs.t: D.S.D. — Summary judgment: uncontroverted facts are deemed admitted
docs.x: D.S.D.. Summary judgment: uncontroverted facts are deemed admitted. The movant files a separate, short, numbered statement of material facts with record cites. The opponent answers each numbered paragraph. Any fact in the movant’s statement not controverted is deemed admitted. (D.S.D. Civ. LR 56.1(A)–(D))

docs.t: D.S.D. — Attorney’s fees: 28 days from judgment or a possible waiver
docs.x: D.S.D.. Attorney’s fees: 28 days from judgment or a possible waiver. Move for fees and file an affidavit of time within 28 calendar days of judgment. Failure to move in time may be treated as a waiver of the claim. (D.S.D. Civ. LR 54.1(C))

docs.t: D.S.D. — Costs: verified bill within 28 days
docs.x: D.S.D.. Costs: verified bill within 28 days. File and serve a verified bill of costs within 28 calendar days after judgment or dismissal. Exceptions are due 14 days after, and a request to review the clerk’s taxation must come within 7 days. (D.S.D. Civ. LR 54.1(A))

docs.t: D.S.D. — Discovery motions need a separate good-faith certification
docs.x: D.S.D.. Discovery motions need a separate good-faith certification. File a separate certification describing the parties’ good-faith efforts to resolve the dispute. If a hearing is set, file a statement of the issues you could not resolve at least 7 calendar days before it. (D.S.D. Civ. LR 37.1)

docs.t: D.S.D. — Oral argument only by order, and you have to ask in time
docs.x: D.S.D.. Oral argument only by order, and you have to ask in time. Ask in a separate statement at the end of the motion or responsive brief, or in a separate document within 14 calendar days after filing the motion or responsive brief. (D.S.D. Civ. LR 7.1(C))

docs.t: D.S.D. — Witness lists are sealed and due by noon the day before trial

docs.x: S.D. Ill.. Thirty days to respond to dispositive motions; fourteen for the rest. docs.t: M.D. Fla. — Response in 14 days, but 21 for the big motions
docs.x: M.D. Fla.. Response in 14 days, but 21 for the big motions. The response is due 14 days after service. It is 21 days for a motion to dismiss, for judgment on the pleadings, for summary judgment, to exclude or limit expert testimony, to certify a class, for a new trial, or to alter or amend a judgment. docs.t: M.D. Fla. — Sealing takes a real motion

docs.t: S.D. Fla. — Rule changes take effect December 1, 2026
docs.x: S.D. Fla.. Rule changes take effect December 1, 2026. Default judgment motions lose their no-memorandum exemption and need a full package (new L.R. 7.1(a)(3)); the conferral rule moves to 7.1(a)(4); pro hac vice certifications must disclose any past suspension (Attorney Rule 4(b)(1)); and new L.R. 7.4 applies the federal Supplemental Rules to individual Social Security review cases. Anything filed on or after December 1 follows the new text. (Admin. Order 2026-94)

docs.t: S.D. Fla. — Fee motions have their own procedure
docs.x: S.D. Fla.. Fee motions have their own procedure. File within 60 days of the final judgment, even if an appeal is pending. At least 30 days before that deadline, serve (don’t file) a draft motion. Within 21 days the parties must confer, and the opposing side must spell out its objections in writing, item by item, with authority. Courts treat objections not made in that process as waived. The motion must be verified and detailed. Bills of costs are due in 30 days. (L.R. 7.3)

docs.t: S.D. Fla. — Discovery disputes have a 28-day deadline
docs.x: S.D. Fla.. Discovery disputes have a 28-day deadline. Raise a discovery dispute within 28 days of the event that caused it, or risk losing it. Most magistrate judges require a discovery hearing or joint motion under their standing orders instead of a written motion. (L.R. 26.1(g))

docs.t: S.D. Fla. — Pre-filing conference and certificate
docs.x: S.D. Fla.. Pre-filing conference and certificate. Before most motions, confer with everyone affected and certify it. Motions to dismiss, for injunctive relief, judgment on the pleadings, and summary judgment are among the exceptions. Judges strike motions missing the certificate. (L.R. 7.1(a)(3) (7.1(a)(4) from Dec. 1, 2026))

docs.t: S.D. Fla. — Local counsel does the filing
docs.x: S.D. Fla.. Local counsel does the filing. Pro hac vice lawyers can’t e-file; local counsel files the motion, pays the fee and files everything after. (Attorney Rule 4(b))

docs.t: S.D. Fla. — One 20-page document; replies are 10 and rebuttal only
docs.x: S.D. Fla.. One 20-page document; replies are 10 and rebuttal only. A motion and its memorandum are a single document, and neither it nor the opposing memorandum may exceed 20 pages without prior permission. A reply is capped at 10 pages and strictly limited to rebutting matters in the opposition. The caption, tables, signature block, and certificates don’t count. (L.R. 7.1(a)(1), (c)(2))

docs.t: S.D. Fla. — Opposition in 14 days, reply in 7, or the motion may be granted by default
docs.x: S.D. Fla.. Opposition in 14 days, reply in 7, or the motion may be granted by default. The opposing memorandum is due 14 days after service, and failing to file one may be sufficient cause to grant the motion by default. The movant has 7 days after the opposition to reply. For a motion served with the summons and complaint, the opposition is due when the response to the complaint is due. (L.R. 7.1(c)(1))

docs.t: S.D. Fla. — Summary judgment needs separate statements of fact
docs.x: S.D. Fla.. Summary judgment needs separate statements of fact. File a Statement of Material Facts as a separate document of no more than 10 pages, in numbered paragraphs, each fact with a pinpoint record cite. The opponent responds the same way and may add up to 5 pages of “Additional Facts,” and the movant then files a reply statement. (L.R. 56.1)

docs.t: S.D. Fla. — Tell the court within two court days when a case settles
docs.x: S.D. Fla.. Tell the court within two court days when a case settles. File a joint notice of settlement within 2 court days after the agreement is reached, or a Rule 41 notice. For a settled jury case, the clerk and judge must hear at least one full business day before jury selection, or juror costs can be assessed. (L.R. 16.4)

docs.t: S.D. Fla. — Sealing: move first, and attach nothing
docs.x: S.D. Fla.. Sealing: move first, and attach nothing. File a public motion describing the material with as much particularity as possible without revealing it, and state the proposed duration. The proposed sealed material isn’t filed unless the court grants the motion. (L.R. 5.4(b)(1))

docs.t: S.D. Fla. — 12-point type and 1½-line spacing
docs.x: S.D. Fla.. 12-point type and 1½-line spacing. Type must be at least 12 points, footnotes and quotations included. Lines are spaced at least 1½, except quotations of 50 words or more and footnotes, which may be single-spaced. Number pages consecutively at the bottom center, and use one side of the paper only. (L.R. 5.1(a)(4))

docs.t: S.D. Fla. — Most magistrate judges bar written discovery motions
docs.x: S.D. Fla.. Most magistrate judges bar written discovery motions. The local rule’s ten-page motion process applies only if the assigned judge’s procedures don’t say otherwise, and they usually do. Judges Torres, Strauss, Reinhart, Hernandez, and Shaw-Wilder bar or strictly control written discovery motions and use a hearing request instead, while Judges Louis, Sanchez, McCabe, and Augustin-Birch permit short motions with set page limits. Read the paired magistrate judge’s procedures before any dispute. (L.R. 26.1(g)(1); judges’ procedures)

docs.t: S.D. Fla. — Deposition rulings: no calls, no instant relief
docs.x: S.D. Fla.. Deposition rulings: no calls, no instant relief. Judge McCabe won’t take calls for immediate rulings during a deposition, Judge Louis says the same, and Judge Torres requires a notice of objection served within five days after you receive a deposition notice. Raise deposition disputes by the judge’s process afterward. (Judges’ procedures)

docs.t: D. Nev. — Pro hac vice is due within 14 days
docs.x: D. Nev.. Pro hac vice is due within 14 days. File the complete verified petition within 14 days of your first appearance: verified (sworn) on the clerk’s form, with good-standing certificates (issued within six months) from every state where you’re admitted, the fee, and a designation of resident counsel with a Nevada office. Until it’s granted you can’t do anything beyond the first filing, and that filing must say you “has complied” or “will comply with LR IA 11-2 within ___ days.” Miss it and the court can strike everything you filed. docs.x: D. Nev.. Not opposing a motion counts as consent. Failing to file points and authorities opposing a motion consents to granting it (summary judgment and fee motions excepted). A movant who files no points and authorities consents to denial. Calendar every opposition. (LR 7-2(d))

docs.t: D. Nev. — Email doesn’t count as meeting and conferring
docs.x: D. Nev.. Email doesn’t count as meeting and conferring. Wherever the rules require you to meet and confer, it has to be direct dialogue: in person, by phone or by video. Letters and email chains don’t satisfy it, and the court can sanction you. (LR IA 1-3(f))

docs.t: D. Nev. — Discovery runs on a short default clock
docs.x: D. Nev.. Discovery runs on a short default clock. Plaintiff must set the Rule 26(f) conference within 30 days after the first defendant answers or appears, and the stipulated discovery plan is due 14 days later. Discovery longer than 180 days from that first appearance needs “special scheduling review.” Extension requests must reach the court at least 21 days before the deadline, or show good cause (and excusable neglect if the deadline has passed). (LR 26-1; LR 26-3)

docs.t: D. Nev. — Filing deadline: 11:59 p.m. Pacific
docs.x: D. Nev.. Filing deadline: 11:59 p.m. Pacific. Unless the court orders otherwise, a document due by a rule or order deadline must be filed by 11:59 p.m. on the date due, measured by the date and time on the Notice of Electronic Filing in the court’s time zone. The deadline printed in a Notice of Electronic Filing is only a courtesy; the court order or the rules control. If a technical failure makes you late, you may ask for relief. Some judges set an earlier time in their standing orders, so check yours. (LR IC 3-1(a))

docs.t: D.N.J. — Motions run on motion days
docs.x: D.N.J.. Motions run on motion days. Motion days are the first and third Mondays. A motion is returnable on the first motion day at least 24 days after filing; opposition is due 14 days before that day and reply 7 days before. Put the motion day on the brief’s cover. (L.Civ.R. 7.1(c), 78.1)

docs.x: D.N.J.. Pro hac vice lawyers can’t file anything. Only a member of this court’s bar may file papers, enter appearances, sign stipulations, or sign and receive payments on judgments. Pro hac lawyers can’t register as ECF filers. (L.Civ.R. 101.1(c)(4))

docs.x: D.N.J.. Discovery disputes go to the magistrate judge by letter or call first. Confer, then present the dispute to the magistrate judge by letter or phone conference before any formal motion. Case management disputes work the same way (L.Civ.R. 16.1(f)). (L.Civ.R. 37.1(a))

docs.t: D.N.J. — Opposing a dispositive motion? You can adjourn it once, by letter
docs.x: D.N.J.. Opposing a dispositive motion? You can adjourn it once, by letter. Before your opposition is due, file and serve a letter stating the motion day hasn’t been adjourned before and invoking the rule. The motion moves to the next available motion day, opposition is then due 14 days before it, and the reply 7 days before. Any other extension takes a court order. (L.Civ.R. 7.1(d)(5))

docs.x: D.N.J.. No statement of facts, no summary judgment. A summary judgment motion without a separate statement of material facts is dismissed. docs.x: S.D.N.Y.. Judges’ own rules change the Local Rules. Most S.D.N.Y. judges require a pre-motion letter and often a conference before motions to dismiss, for summary judgment or on discovery. docs.t: S.D.N.Y. — Words, not pages
docs.x: S.D.N.Y.. Words, not pages. Briefs in support and opposition: 8,750 words. Replies: 3,500. Include a certificate of compliance with the word count. (Local Civ. R. 7.1(c))

docs.t: S.D.N.Y. — Rule 56.1 statements
docs.x: S.D.N.Y.. Rule 56.1 statements. Summary judgment requires a separate statement of undisputed facts in numbered paragraphs, each cited to admissible evidence. The opponent answers paragraph by paragraph; anything not specifically controverted is deemed admitted. (Local Civ. R. 56.1)

docs.t: S.D.N.Y. — Early interrogatories are restricted
docs.x: S.D.N.Y.. Early interrogatories are restricted. At the start of discovery, interrogatories are limited to basics like witness names, documents and damages. Contention interrogatories wait until the end of discovery. Lawyers from elsewhere who serve broad first-wave interrogatories draw objections. (Local Civ. R. 33.3)

docs.t: S.D.N.Y. — Filing deadline: midnight, local time
docs.x: S.D.N.Y.. Filing deadline: midnight, local time. On the last day, an electronic filing is timely until midnight in the court’s time zone. Paper filings are due when the clerk’s office is scheduled to close. Some judges set an earlier time in their standing orders, so check yours. (Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(a)(4)(A))

docs.t: N.D. Ohio — Your case track sets your page limits
docs.x: N.D. Ohio. Your case track sets your page limits. Dispositive motion memoranda: 10 pages on the expedited track, 20 on standard and administrative, 30 on complex, 40 on mass tort. Find the track in the case management order before you outline. (L.R. 7.1(f); L.R. 16.2)

docs.t: N.D. Ohio — Long briefs need a full front section
docs.x: N.D. Ohio. Long briefs need a full front section. Memoranda over the short limit must include a table of contents, table of authorities, a brief statement of the issues, and a summary of the argument. (L.R. 7.1(f))

docs.t: N.D. Ohio — Tell the judge before you file a discovery motion
docs.x: N.D. Ohio. Tell the judge before you file a discovery motion. Confer first. If that fails, notify the judicial officer, who may hold a phone conference, and then ask for letters. Memoranda come only on a date the judge sets. (L.R. 37.1)

docs.t: S.D. Ohio — Every party needs a Trial Attorney from this bar
docs.x: S.D. Ohio. Every party needs a Trial Attorney from this bar. The Trial Attorney is responsible for the case. A pro hac lawyer can’t serve in that role unless the court permits it for good cause, so out-of-state counsel needs a permanent member of this bar on the case. (S.D. Ohio Civ. R. 83.3(f); 83.4(a))

docs.t: S.D. Ohio — No memoranda beyond the reply without leave
docs.x: S.D. Ohio. No memoranda beyond the reply without leave. Opposition, then reply within 14 days. Anything more requires leave for good cause. (S.D. Ohio Civ. R. 7.2(a)(2))

docs.t: S.D. Ohio — Briefs over 20 pages need a summary
docs.x: S.D. Ohio. Briefs over 20 pages need a summary. Memoranda longer than 20 pages need a combined table of contents and a summary of no more than five pages. Some divisions (Dayton) add more requirements. (S.D. Ohio Civ. R. 7.2(a)(3))

docs.t: S.D. Ohio — Exhaust everything before a discovery motion
docs.x: S.D. Ohio. Exhaust everything before a discovery motion. Discovery motions can’t be filed until the parties exhaust all extrajudicial means. Then, instead of a motion, you can ask for an informal discovery dispute conference with the judge. (S.D. Ohio Civ. R. 37.1)
